title: Line chart
description:
A line chart draws one or more series over an x axis: `x_column` and `y_column` (or
`y_columns`, or `series_column` for long data). The default is a braille canvas; the
style rule `chart { canvas }` picks another pixel grid and `chart { renderer: asciichart }`
draws box lines.
See `:help dbdash-charts`.

query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE h(n) AS (SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM h WHERE n < 23)
SELECT printf('%02d:00', n) AS hour, 60 + 40 * sin(n / 3.0) + abs(random() % 20) AS visits,
       (60 + 40 * sin(n / 3.0)) * 0.6 AS mobile, (60 + 40 * sin(n / 3.0)) * 0.4 AS desktop
FROM h

show.title: y_columns, legend, axes (canvas: braille, the default)
show.description:
Three series from `y_columns`, each with a `label`, colored by `series.<label>`
rules; the legend sits on the `right` (default) or `bottom` (`legend { position }`);
`axes.y_axis` sets a title, `min_value` and a Python `format` for the tick labels.
Braille draws 2 x 4 dots per character.

query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE h(n) AS (SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM h WHERE n < 23)
SELECT printf('%02d', n) AS hour, 60 + 40 * sin(n / 3.0) AS visits FROM h

show.title: chart { canvas: quadrant }
show.description: `chart { canvas: quadrant }`: 2 x 2 pixels per character (▗▄▖), works in most fonts.

query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE h(n) AS (SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM h WHERE n < 23)
SELECT printf('%02d', n) AS hour, 60 + 40 * sin(n / 3.0) AS visits FROM h

show.title: chart { canvas: block }
show.description: `chart { canvas: block }`: one full block per pixel (coarse but bold).

query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE h(n) AS (SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM h WHERE n < 23)
SELECT printf('%02d', n) AS hour, 60 + 40 * sin(n / 3.0) AS visits FROM h

show.title: chart { canvas: halfblock }
show.description: `chart { canvas: halfblock }`: 1 x 2 pixels per character (▀ ▄).

query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE h(n) AS (SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM h WHERE n < 23)
SELECT printf('%02d', n) AS hour, 60 + 40 * sin(n / 3.0) AS visits FROM h

show.title: chart { canvas: ascii }
show.description: `chart { canvas: ascii }`: plain ASCII characters, for any terminal or font.

query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE h(n) AS (SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM h WHERE n < 23)
SELECT printf('%02d', n) AS hour, 60 + 40 * sin(n / 3.0) AS visits FROM h

show.title: chart { renderer: asciichart }
show.description:
`chart { renderer: asciichart }` draws the line with box characters (╭─╯) instead of a
pixel canvas. Try it on any line chart with `:DbDashStyle line asciichart`.

query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE d(n) AS (SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM d WHERE n < 13)
SELECT printf('%02d', n) AS day, k AS region, 50 + abs(random() % 50) AS orders
FROM d, (SELECT 'EU' AS k UNION ALL SELECT 'US' UNION ALL SELECT 'APAC')

show.title: series_column: long data
show.description:
Long data (one row per x and series) with `series_column`: one line per value of
`region`, colored from the palette (`chart { palette: tableau }` here; `theme`
follows the colorscheme); `legend { position: bottom }` puts the legend below.

query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE h(n) AS (SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM h WHERE n < 11)
SELECT n AS x, 20 + 15 * sin(n / 2.0) AS y FROM h

show.title: series { fill }, point { display: block }
show.description: `series { fill: true }` fills under the line (Chart.js `fill`); `point { display: block }` marks every point.

query.sql:
SELECT 1 AS t, 3 AS level UNION ALL SELECT 2, 3 UNION ALL SELECT 3, 7 UNION ALL SELECT 4, 5
UNION ALL SELECT 5, 9 UNION ALL SELECT 6, 9 UNION ALL SELECT 7, 4

show.title: series { curve: step-after }
show.description:
Steps instead of slopes (Chart.js `stepped`): `curve: step` / `step-before` (the
value changes at the start), `step-after`, `step-middle`. Good for states and
counters.

query.sql:
SELECT 1 AS t, 4 AS v UNION ALL SELECT 2, 6 UNION ALL SELECT 3, NULL UNION ALL SELECT 4, NULL
UNION ALL SELECT 5, 8 UNION ALL SELECT 6, 5 UNION ALL SELECT 7, 7

show.title: point { content }, span_gaps: false
show.description:
`point { display: block, content: "●" }` marks each point with a character (Chart.js
`pointStyle`); `span_gaps: false` leaves a gap where the value is NULL instead of
joining across it.

query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE h(n) AS (SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM h WHERE n < 11)
SELECT n AS month, round(power(2.4, n)) AS users FROM h

show.title: axes: scale: log, ticks; grid lines
show.subtitle: users per month, log scale
show.description:
A log y axis (Chart.js `type: logarithmic`) for growth over orders of magnitude;
`ticks` asks for about that many x ticks, `grid.x` / `grid.y { display: block }` draw
grid lines at the ticks.
`subtitle` adds a muted line under the title.

query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE h(n) AS (SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM h WHERE n < 23)
SELECT printf('%02d', n) AS hour, 50 + 30 * sin(n / 4.0) + abs(random() % 15) AS latency FROM h

show.title: mark_lines, mark_points
show.description:
Reference lines (ECharts `markLine`): a fixed value with a label, or `mean`, `min`,
`max` of the data, on the `y` (default) or `x` axis; a line's `class` styles it
(`mark.slo { color }`). `mark_points` labels each series' `max` and `min` (ECharts
`markPoint`).

query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE h(n) AS (SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM h WHERE n < 23)
SELECT printf('%02d', n) AS hour, 60 + 40 * sin(n / 3.0) AS visits FROM h

show.title: x_label, y_label; plot height, chart max-width, no legend
show.description:
`x_label` / `y_label` are short for the axis titles; `plot { height }` fixes the plot
rows, `chart { max-width }` caps the chart width; `legend { display: none }` hides
the legend.
